fromStream Behavior

withCoreFromStreamBehavior is a FeatureCell API extension behavior that integrates observable event streams into a FeatureCell by subscribing to a source stream and injecting emitted values into the pipeline as state updates.

This behavior operates outside of the pipeline and does not participate in Resolve, operator, filter, or reducer stages directly. Instead, it resolves values externally and forwards them into the pipeline using standard state update mechanisms, where they are normalized and committed by core resolve and state behaviors.

withCoreFromStreamBehavior was originally developed to support the Chrome DevTools app and internal EventBus integration, where high-frequency events must be observed, monitored, and reflected in state without incurring excessive pipeline orchestration overhead. This design allows continuous or noisy event sources to be piped efficiently into a FeatureCell.

This behavior extends the FeatureCell instance by adding a fromStream() method directly to the cell API.

When fromStream() is invoked, the behavior establishes a subscription to the provided observable and injects each emitted value into the FeatureCell as a state update. These injected updates are forwarded through the normal pipeline, where they are normalized by the Resolve stage and committed by the State stage.

Subscription lifecycle is bound to the FeatureCell lifecycle. Active subscriptions are automatically terminated when the FeatureCell is reset or destroyed, ensuring that stream-driven updates cannot outlive the owning cell or produce orphaned state emissions.

Note

When reset() is called, the StateSnapshotShape.value is set to undefined. If the FeatureCell relies on an array-based merge behavior (such as append or push), the value must be restored to an empty array before stream emissions can accumulate correctly.

After calling reset(), you should reinitialize the state with: 


vault.replaceState([]);

This ensures that subsequent stream emissions have a valid array target for merge semantics.

Note

When using fromStream(), it is strongly recommended to register an appropriate merge behavior for the FeatureCell.

Stream-based inputs emit values over time. Without a merge strategy that accumulates or augments existing state, each emission will overwrite the previous value—making the stream semantically equivalent to repeated replaceState() calls.

To preserve the intent of streaming data—such as event logs, collections, or incremental updates—use a merge behavior designed for additive semantics:

  • withArrayAppendMergeBehavior — appends each emitted value to an array
  • withArrayPushMergeBehavior — pushes emitted values into an existing array

These merge behaviors ensure that each stream emission contributes meaningfully to the accumulated state rather than discarding prior values.

Diagram
Configuration

withCoreFromStreamBehavior withCoreFromStreamBehavior is configured by invoking the fromStream() method on an initialized FeatureCell. Calling this method establishes a long-lived subscription to an observable source and forwards emitted values into the FeatureCell as state updates.

Unlike resolve behaviors that execute within the pipeline, this behavior operates outside of pipeline execution. Stream emissions are injected into the pipeline using standard state update mechanisms, where they are normalized and committed by the Resolve and State stages.

Configuration is supplied at the point of subscription using the fromStream(source$, options) API. The subscription remains active for the lifetime of the FeatureCell and is automatically terminated on reset or destruction.

Configuration Options
Option Description
autoResetError?: boolean When enabled (default), each successful stream emission clears any existing error state before injecting the new value into the pipeline. When disabled, prior error state is preserved until explicitly cleared by a subsequent state update.
Registering the fromStream Behavior

The fromStream Behavior is a core behavior and does not need to be attached structurally when the FeatureCell is defined.

FeatureCell Stream Integration

withCoreFromStreamBehavior extends the FeatureCell instance with a fromStream() method, enabling observable streams to act as continuous state update sources for the cell.

Unlike replaceState and mergeState, which submit discrete state updates, fromStream() establishes a long-lived subscription to an observable and injects each emitted value into the FeatureCell as a state update.

This method does not perform resolution itself. Each emitted value is converted into a standard state input and forwarded through the normal pipeline, where it is normalized by the Resolve stage and finalized by the State stage.

Extended FeatureCell API
API Description

.fromStream(source$, options?)

inputs:

  • source$: Observable<T>
  • options?: FromStreamOptions

returns:

  • void

Subscribes to an observable source and forwards each emitted value into the FeatureCell as a state update. Emissions are injected using standard pipeline admission and are normalized by the Resolve stage before downstream processing.

The subscription is bound to the FeatureCell lifecycle. It is automatically terminated on reset or destruction, ensuring that stream-driven updates cannot outlive the owning FeatureCell.

This API is intended for continuous or high-frequency event sources, such as event buses, DevTools instrumentation, WebSocket feeds, or other long-lived observable streams.

Common Use Cases

withCoreFromStreamBehavior is designed for scenarios where values are produced continuously over time and must be reflected in state as they occur. Rather than submitting discrete updates, this behavior bridges live streams directly into the FeatureCell lifecycle.

In all cases, fromStream() focuses solely on connection and lifecycle management. Each emitted value is injected as a standard state update and resolved through the normal pipeline, ensuring consistent behavior across all downstream stages.

Typical Use Cases
Use Case Description
DevTools Event Streams Originally designed to support DevTools, this behavior efficiently pipes high-frequency internal events directly into a FeatureCell without overwhelming the pipeline with repeated manual updates.
Application Event Bus Connects an application-wide event bus or message stream to state, allowing events to be observed, accumulated, or reacted to as part of normal pipeline processing.
WebSocket Feeds Ideal for real-time data sources such as WebSockets or SSE streams, where each message should immediately update or augment state.
User Interaction Streams Useful for continuous UI signals such as cursor movement, drag events, gesture tracking, or high-frequency input streams that should flow directly into state.
Logging and Diagnostics Streams diagnostic messages, warnings, or trace events into state for inspection, visualization, or debugging purposes.
Incremental Collection Building When paired with array-based merge behaviors, stream emissions can be accumulated into lists, queues, or histories without manual coordination.
External Library Integration Adapts third-party observable APIs into the FeatureCell model without modifying or wrapping their emission logic.
Cross-Feature Coordination Allows one FeatureCell to react to state or events emitted by another cell via observable bridges, enabling loosely coupled coordination.
Monitoring & Telemetry Streams metrics, counters, or performance signals into state for dashboards, alerts, or analytics.
Examples

withCoreFromStreamBehavior enables observable streams to be connected directly to a FeatureCell via the fromStream() API. This method establishes a subscription that continuously injects emitted values into the pipeline as state updates.

In the examples below, a FeatureCell is initialized normally. After initialization, an observable stream is attached using fromStream(). Each emitted value is converted into a standard state update and forwarded through the Resolve stage before being finalized by the State stage.

Example 1: Stream Values into a FeatureCell

{{`@FeatureCell<Employee[]>('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[]>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();

    // Observable defined locally in the cell
    const employees$ = of([
      { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
    ]);

    // Stream values directly into the FeatureCell
    this.vault.fromStream(employees$);
  }
}`}}
 
{{`import { of } from 'rxjs';

export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  }
);

employeeCell.initialize();

// Observable defined locally in the module
const employees$ = of([
  { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
  { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
]);

// Stream values directly into the FeatureCell
employeeCell.fromStream(employees$);`}}
